traceability.notes:
The story 003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS is fully implemented and verified.
• Core Functionality (require-story-annotation & require-req-annotation): - Both rules enforce their respective annotations on the same shared set of function-like constructs: FunctionDeclaration, FunctionExpression, MethodDefinition, TSDeclareFunction, TSMethodSignature. This set is defined centrally in DEFAULT_SCOPE in src/rules/helpers/require-story-core.ts and consumed by both rules via shouldProcessNode in src/rules/helpers/require-story-helpers.ts. - Arrow functions are explicitly implemented for @story but excluded from enforcement by default because ArrowFunctionExpression is not present in DEFAULT_SCOPE and is disallowed by the schema for the scope option. Tests confirm that unannotated arrow functions are allowed by default while annotated arrows are accepted.
• JSDoc Parsing & Error Handling: - For @story, hasStoryAnnotation combines multiple heuristics: JSDoc (`getJSDocComment`), comments before node (`getCommentsBefore`), leadingComments, lookback line scan, parent-chain scan, and a bounded fallback text window, all guarded with type checks and try/catch so malformed or missing JSDoc/comments do not throw. This matches REQ-JSDOC-PARSING and the error-handling acceptance criterion. - For @req, checkReqAnnotation and hasReqAnnotation use analogous heuristics (JSDoc + combined comments, then line/parent/fallback checks) with similar guards and try/catch. Failure to read comments or source is treated as “no annotation” but does not break linting, satisfying graceful error handling.
• Annotation Requirements & Configurable Scope: - When in scope (as determined by DEFAULT_SCOPE and the optional scope and exportPriority options), require-story-annotation reports a missing @story via messageId "missingStory" and provides an autofix and suggestion; require-req-annotation reports missing @req via "missingReq" and, via the shared checker, can also provide autofixes where enabled. - Both rules accept the same options structure and semantics: a scope array restricted to the shared function-like node types and an exportPriority option ('all' | 'exported' | 'non-exported'). Both use shouldProcessNode to interpret these consistently, so the same configuration yields the same set of in-scope nodes for both rules.
• Export Priority & Error Location: - isExportedNode in require-story-helpers walks the parent chain to detect ExportNamedDeclaration and ExportDefaultDeclaration, and shouldProcessNode interprets exportPriority consistently for both rules. Tests for both rules validate that exported vs non-exported functions/methods are enforced or ignored as configured. - Error locations are anchored at the most specific identifier/key node available (function id or method key), both for @story and @req, satisfying REQ-ERROR-LOCATION. Test cases include data payload checks (`{ name, functionName }`) that indirectly confirm correct name resolution.
• TypeScript Support: - Both rules include explicit visitors for TSDeclareFunction and TSMethodSignature and are exercised using @typescript-eslint/parser via shared TS RuleTester language options. Additional helpers (annotation-checker and reqAnnotationDetection) are designed to be parser-agnostic but are tested specifically with TS constructs. Tests confirm behavior for TS interface method signatures and declare functions, fully satisfying REQ-TYPESCRIPT-SUPPORT.
• Documentation & UX: - Dedicated rule docs in docs/rules/require-story-annotation.md and docs/rules/require-req-annotation.md describe behavior, supported node types, configuration options, and examples, matching the story’s requirements and acceptance criteria for documentation. - Error messages are explicit and actionable, instructing developers to add @story or @req annotations, with concrete examples and clear indication of the required remediation, meeting the user-experience acceptance criterion.
Given the implemented rules, shared helpers, comprehensive RuleTester coverage for both JavaScript and TypeScript across the specified node types and configuration options, and passing Jest test suite, all acceptance criteria and detailed requirements of docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md are satisfied. Therefore this story is assessed as PASSED.
